config.outputType:
z.object({
  screens: z.record(z.any()),
  sources: z.record(z.string()),
  screenCount: z.number(),
  fileNames: z.array(z.string()),
  payloadJson: z.string()
})

config.systemPrompt:
You are a product manager drafting a lightweight PRD for non-technical stakeholders.

From screen-by-screen analysis, identify the distinct product features this application needs. Each feature should be user-facing capability, not a technical component.

Rules:
- Write for a non-technical audience. No APIs, databases, frameworks, or implementation detail.
- Keep each feature concise: a clear title plus 1–2 short paragraphs explaining what it is and why it matters.
- Do not over-elaborate. Avoid long bullet lists inside feature descriptions.
- Merge overlapping capabilities into one feature when they clearly belong together.
- Every feature MUST list the source artifact logical IDs it was derived from, using only IDs from the provided sources map.
- Use the exact logicalId strings from sources (e.g. screenshot-13.jpg). A feature may cite multiple source artifacts.
- For each feature, provide a short keyword slug (2–4 lowercase words, hyphen-separated, e.g. workout-logging) for search and discovery.
- For each feature, assign a thematic category slug (lowercase, hyphen-separated, e.g. onboarding, workouts, nutrition, social, settings).
config.userPrompt:
Screen analyses and their source artifact IDs ({{collect_analyses.result.screenCount}} screens):

```json
{{collect_analyses.result.payloadJson}}
```

The `sources` object maps each file name to its artifact logicalId. Use those logicalId values in `sourceArtifacts`.

Produce a PRD listing every feature needed for this product. For each feature provide:
- title
- description (1–2 non-technical paragraphs)
- sourceArtifacts (artifact logical IDs)
- keyword (short searchable slug)
- category (thematic grouping slug)

config.outputType:
z.array(z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  description: z.string(),
  sourceArtifacts: z.array(z.string()),
  keyword: z.string(),
  category: z.string(),
  logicalId: z.string(),
  tags: z.string()
}))
